title: fix(plugin-grid): one presence rule for `pagination` and `selection` — presence enables, an explicit off wins
body:
Fixes #9837

Ruling batch #162 item 2, letter A-prime, maintainer 「同意」 (objectui#9837 comment 5729875984). `object-grid`'s two adjacent object-armed keys now read their own presence by the SAME rule: **presence enables the feature with the object's settings, and an explicit off wins over presence.**

## What moved

Both reads live in the one props fold that assembles `dataTableSchema`, and until now they disagreed about what writing the object means:

- `pagination` was read as `!== undefined` FIRST, which hard-forced paging on and made the deprecated flat `showPagination: false` unreachable the moment the object was written — a block that cannot turn off the thing it names (the objectui#9819 shape).
- `selection` was read as the optional-chained `type`, so an object with no `type` member did nothing at all and fell straight through to the legacy `selectable` arm.

| authored | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `pagination: { … }` + `showPagination: false` | paging ON | paging OFF |
| `selection: {}` (no `type`) | selection OFF — the legacy arm decided | selection ON, multiple |
| `pagination: { … }` alone | paging ON | paging ON (unchanged) |
| `selection: { type: 'none' }` | selection OFF | selection OFF (unchanged) |
| `selection: { type: 'none' }` + `selectable: true` | selection OFF | selection OFF (unchanged) |

The order of the two arms is the whole ruling on the `pagination` side. That key declares no off member of its own (`pageSize` / `pageSizeOptions`), so the deprecated flat boolean is the only off an author has and it has to be read BEFORE the object's presence. On the `selection` side the canonical off lives INSIDE the object (`type: 'none'`), so the legacy `selectable` keeps its existing standing: read only when `selection` is absent.

`selection: {}` resolves to `multiple` through a named constant. That value is derived, not chosen: the ruling's first clause is that writing the object turns selection ON, so `'none'` is excluded outright, and `'multiple'` is already this renderer's own answer to "selection is on, nothing said which kind" — it is what the bulk-action auto-enable arm resolves to and what the legacy `selectable: true` means. `'single'` would have been a third, unstated opinion.

## The two member pins, flipped on purpose

`gridPagerSelectionMembers-8071.test.tsx` pinned both retired readings deliberately (objectui#8071 slice 13, PR objectui#9836), so they had to move. Both `describe` blocks now carry the one sentence, and the file's own docblock NAMES the retired rule rather than being quietly rewritten — a reader who meets the old behaviour in a half-migrated page needs to know it was retired.

- `the OBJECT's presence enables paging, overruling showPagination: false` became `an explicit showPagination: false turns paging OFF beside the OBJECT`, with the same fixture and the opposite expectation.
- The `selection` describe asserted "only `type` is read". It gained `the OBJECT's presence enables selection with no type member written`, plus a non-vacuity control showing the same schema with no object renders no checkbox at all.
- One more control was added on the pagination side: the same object WITHOUT the off still pages, so "no pager" in the two rows above is the boolean's doing and not the fixture's.

⚠️ The presence clause on `pagination` is INERT today and deliberately has no row of its own: paging already defaults ON, so an authored `pagination: {}` and an absent `pagination` are indistinguishable at the pager. The observable half of the rule on that key is the explicit off, and that is what is pinned. This is stated in the file's docblock rather than left for a reader to rediscover.

## Reverse verification

Both new readings were ablated from the COMMITTED tree through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which proves the mutation landed on disk (anchor count and blob hash) and proves the restore (`blob == HEAD` and `git diff HEAD` empty) rather than trusting an exit code. The suite resolves `ObjectGrid` by relative import from source, so there is no build step between the mutation and the reading.

| mutation | blob | result |
|---|---|---|
| pagination read restored to `schema.pagination !== undefined` first | `6808a78e65fb` to `495fc0210fe6` | 1 failed, 14 passed — exactly `an explicit showPagination: false turns paging OFF beside the OBJECT` |
| selection guard restored to `if (schema.selection?.type)` | `6808a78e65fb` to `1236d7a1535f` | 1 failed, 14 passed — exactly `the OBJECT's presence enables selection with no type member written` |

Each restore leg reported `blob == HEAD (6808a78e65fb)` with an empty `git diff HEAD`. Both mutations are one-shot proofs; nothing from them is left in the tree.

A refusal is not a derivation, and it is named here rather than reported as one.

## Acceptance notes

Observations found while doing this, none filed and none fixed here:

- `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` carries the `MEMBER_PINS` ledger, whose `object-grid.pagination` and `object-grid.selection` `pins` prose still DESCRIBES the retired readings ("`pagination !== undefined` is what enables paging, so an authored object OVERRULES a deprecated `showPagination: false`"; "the OBJECT's presence alone does nothing"), as does the slice-13 docblock further down the same file. That prose is reviewed rather than computed — nothing asserts it, which is why the console suite is green above — so it goes stale silently the moment this lands. It is outside the file surface this branch declared, so it is named here for the reviewer rather than edited in.
- `packages/plugin-view/src/__tests__/ObjectView.canonicalTableKeys.test.tsx` justifies its "leave the canonical slot empty when only the legacy key is written" row with the comment "`ObjectGrid` keys `paginationEnabled` off `schema.pagination !== undefined`, so a synthesised `pagination` would turn pagination on for legacy authors". The assertion stays right and stays green; only its stated reason moves.
- `packages/plugin-grid/README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx` both carry the row "`{ pageSize?, pageSizeOptions? }` — strict, and its presence is what enables paging". Still true after this change and therefore not a falsified claim, but incomplete: neither mentions that an explicit `showPagination: false` beats the object. Both are outside this branch's declared file surface. The sentence they would gain is the one now carried by the `pagination` input's `description` in `packages/plugin-grid/src/index.tsx`.

## Open question for the reviewer

`@objectstack/spec`'s `SelectionConfigSchema` declares `type` with a `'none'` DEFAULT of its own. This repository's mirror strips imported defaults at the import boundary, so an omitted `type` stays omitted on the way to the renderer and A-prime's presence clause is reachable here. But metadata that was parsed by the spec bundle BEFORE reaching the renderer materialises `type: 'none'` and is then read here as an explicit off — so the same authored bytes mean "selection on" or "selection off" depending on whether they were parsed on the way in. A-prime settles the renderer; it does not settle that seam, and settling it is a `@objectstack/spec` decision, not an objectui one. Carried in the report and in the constant's own docblock rather than decided here.
